Name: WUSTL-IIOT-2021
Summary: Network flow records from an IIoT testbed at Washington University in St. Louis with 1,194,464 observations, 41 features and labelled DoS, reconnaissance and injection attacks.
Description:
WUSTL-IIOT-2021 is a dataset for research on AI and ML-based intrusion detection in the Industrial Internet of Things, collected on a testbed developed at Washington University in St. Louis. Command injection, reconnaissance and DoS attacks were generated against the testbed, and attacks were kept under 8% of the traffic so that the data resembles real-world industrial control systems. A related article by M. Zolanvari, R. Jain and co-authors appeared in the IEEE Internet of Things Journal.

The dataset holds 1,194,464 observations described by 41 features that are common in network flows and change during attack phases, such as packet and byte counts, loads, rates, jitter, durations and TCP round-trip time.

Attack traffic makes up 7.28% of the records. Within it, DoS accounts for 89.98%, reconnaissance for 9.46%, command injection for 0.31% and backdoor for 0.25%. The data downloads as a single file of 106,192,911 bytes.
